name: Taj Mahal
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site built by Emperor Shah Jahan in memory of Mumtaz Mahal. Famous for its white marble architecture and intricate craftsmanship.

name: Agra Fort
description: A magnificent red sandstone fort that served as an important residence of Mughal emperors.

name: Fatehpur Sikri
description: A historic Mughal city founded by Emperor Akbar, known for its palaces, courtyards and Buland Darwaza.

name: Qutub Minar
description: A towering brick minaret and UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring Indo-Islamic architectural details.

name: Red Fort
description: A historic Mughal fort built by Shah Jahan. It is the site of India's annual Independence Day address.

name: Humayun's Tomb
description: A grand garden tomb commissioned by Humayun's widow. Its design influenced later Mughal architecture.

name: Amber Fort
description: A hilltop fort known for its grand gateways, mirror work, courtyards and Rajput architecture.

name: Hawa Mahal
description: The Palace of Winds is famous for its honeycomb facade and numerous small windows.

name: Chittorgarh Fort
description: One of India's largest forts, associated with the history and legends of Mewar and Rajput resistance.

name: Jaisalmer Fort
description: A living sandstone fort rising above the Thar Desert, containing homes, temples and historic streets.

name: Konark Sun Temple
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site designed as the monumental stone chariot of the Sun God Surya.

name: Jagannath Temple
description: A major Hindu pilgrimage centre dedicated to Lord Jagannath and renowned for the annual Rath Yatra.

name: Khajuraho Group of Monuments
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site celebrated for its Nagara-style temples and detailed stone sculptures.

name: Sanchi Stupa
description: An important Buddhist monument originally commissioned by Emperor Ashoka and expanded over centuries.

name: Gwalior Fort
description: A dramatic hilltop fort known for its palaces, temples and historic architecture.

name: Ajanta Caves
description: Buddhist rock-cut caves famous for ancient murals, sculptures and religious art.

name: Ellora Caves
description: A remarkable complex of Buddhist, Hindu and Jain monuments carved into volcanic rock.

name: Gateway of India
description: An iconic basalt arch built during the British colonial period overlooking Mumbai Harbour.

name: Hampi Group of Monuments
description: The ruins of the Vijayanagara Empire, featuring temples, royal structures and impressive stone architecture.

name: Mysore Palace
description: The former royal residence of the Wadiyar dynasty, known for its Indo-Saracenic architecture.

name: Group of Monuments at Mahabalipuram
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring Pallava-era rock-cut caves, monolithic temples and stone reliefs.

name: Brihadeeswara Temple
description: A masterpiece of Chola architecture dedicated to Lord Shiva, famous for its monumental vimana.

name: Meenakshi Amman Temple
period: Historic; major expansion in the 16th–17th Century
description: A celebrated temple complex known for its colourful gopurams and elaborate sculptures.

name: Charminar
description: A landmark monument built by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah, recognised for its four grand arches and minarets.

name: Golconda Fort
description: A historic fortress associated with the Qutb Shahi dynasty and the region's diamond trade.

name: Victoria Memorial
description: A white marble memorial and museum built in memory of Queen Victoria, blending European architectural influences.

name: Hazarduari Palace
description: A grand palace built during the Nawabi period, known for its thousand-door design and museum collection.

name: Golden Temple
description: Harmandir Sahib is the central spiritual site of Sikhism, known for its golden sanctum and community kitchen.

name: Rani ki Vav
description: A UNESCO World Heritage Site and intricately decorated stepwell commissioned by Queen Udayamati.

name: Dholavira
description: A major Harappan archaeological site revealing the urban planning, water management and civilisation of the Indus Valley.
